job.title: Recruitment Consultant
job.description:
About the Company
Farrow Jamieson is an executive search and recruitment firm with more than 40 years in the New Zealand market. We are part of the Alpha Group of Companies, which include, Sheffield South Island, Emergent, The Johnson Group, Project Plus, Manamahi, Asset Recruitment, Alpha Recruitment, Triangle Recruitment, Healthwise Personnel and Staffwise.
We have built our longevity on a willingness to keep changing: adopting the best technology we can find globally, testing new approaches and continually improving how we identify and attract talent. Technology matters to us, but people matter more. We never lose sight of the fact that recruitment deals with people's careers, hopes and aspirations.

About  the Role
This is an opportunity for a Recruitment Consultant who wants to become more skilled, effective and commercially capable. You may currently work in a specialist discipline or as a generalist; what matters is your appetite to listen, change, grow and contribute to the team.

You will manage recruitment assignments, build trusted client and candidate relationships, and use contemporary technology and search methods to identify and engage the right people.
Duties
  • Manage recruitment assignments from briefing through to successful appointment.
    • Build enduring relationships with clients and understand what success looks like for them.
    • Identify, approach and engage high-quality candidates using modern search tools and technology.
    • Represent candidates thoughtfully, recognising the importance of career decisions.
    • Contribute ideas, knowledge and effort to the wider Farrow Jamieson team.
    • Keep developing your craft and look for better, faster and more effective ways to work.
Skills & Experience
We are interested in recruitment professionals who can demonstrate:

• Recruitment experience in a specialist discipline or generalist environment.
• Strong listening, communication and relationship-building skills.
• A genuine commitment to client satisfaction and high-quality work.
• Curiosity about technology and new ways of identifying and attracting talent.
• The capacity to accept feedback, change approach and keep developing.
Culture

Farrow Jamieson people do not talk about “hot desks”, “rock stars” or “ninjas”. We talk about client satisfaction, doing great work and enjoying the success that follows.

We are a supportive team that values professional judgement, continuous improvement and shared success. Our expectation is for people to commit to the team as well as their own performance.
Benefits
  • Grow your recruitment career in a supportive, professional, experienced team environment.
    • Use leading technology, sourced globally, to make search and engagement more effective.
    • Join a long-established national firm that continues to evolve.
    • Develop management and leadership skills within Farrow Jamieson or the wider Alpha Group of Companies.
    • Build deeper capability across client management, search, candidate engagement and recruitment delivery.
How to Apply
If you call, be ready to answer two questions: How do you know recruitment is what you want to do as a career? And can you convince us that you will listen, grow and contribute to a highly professional team.

Still want to talk? Click the “APPLY” button to submit your application. For a confidential discussion, contact Iain MacGibbon at Farrow Jamieson on +64 9 915 9144.

job.title: General Manager
job.description:
About the Organisation

Community Law South Auckland (CLSA) is a well-established community law centre providing free legal advice, assistance, representation, mediation and legal education to eligible people across South Auckland, Otahuhu and Franklin. With offices in Otara and Papakura, plus outreach services in Pukekohe and a Māori Land Advisory Clinic, the organisation plays a critical role in improving access to justice for communities that may otherwise struggle to obtain legal support.

CLSA is the largest community law centre by population served and is financially stable, with core Ministry of Justice funding secured through June 2028 and is financially robust. Its long-serving, highly experienced team reflects the communities it serves, with strong Pacific and Māori representation and a deeply embedded commitment to culturally responsive service.

About  the Role

Reporting to the Board of Trustees, the General Manager has overall responsibility for the operational leadership of CLSA and for ensuring the organisation continues to deliver high-quality, accessible and culturally responsive services.

This is a people-centered leadership role rather than a traditional corporate GM position. The successful person will work closely with a highly experienced team of lawyers and support staff, maintain strong community and sector relationships, oversee financial and contractual performance, and help the Board shape the organisation's next strategic chapter.

Early priorities will include building trust with staff and communities, supporting succession planning across a senior workforce, contributing to the next strategic review, and preparing the organisation for future changes in service delivery, technology and AI.

Duties
  • Lead day-to-day operations across CLSA’s Otara and Papakura offices, maintaining an inclusive, culturally safe workplace focused on staff wellbeing and retention.
  • Support the Board with strategic advice, reporting, risk management and implementation of the Strategic Plan.
  • Oversee budgets, financial performance, audit, resources and organisational risk, ensuring funding and contractual obligations are met.
  • Monitor service delivery, community impact and contractual performance while protecting service quality and equitable access to justice.
  • Build trusted relationships across Community Law Centres Aotearoa, government, justice, iwi, hapū, Māori and Pacific organisations, and community providers.
  • Lead succession planning and capability development across the team.
  • Guide practical adoption of technology, data and AI, while remaining visible, accessible and willing to step in operationally when needed.  
Skills & Experience
  • Proven senior leadership experience in a community, social service, public sector, legal, justice or not-for-profit environment.
  • Strong understanding of frontline service delivery to people experiencing disadvantage, complexity or significant life challenges.
  • High emotional intelligence, maturity and judgement, with demonstrated cultural competence and the ability to build trust across diverse groups, including Māori and Pacific communities.
  • Strong people leadership capability, including staff wellbeing, coaching, development, retention and navigating change.
  • Sound financial literacy, budget oversight, risk management and governance reporting experience, including working with Boards, funders, government agencies and external stakeholders.
  • Calm, practical and hands-on leadership style, with confidence managing conflict and challenging situations constructively.
  • Relevant tertiary qualification or equivalent professional experience. Legal qualifications are not required but exposure to government contracting, community law or the justice sector would be advantageous.  
Culture

CLSA has a close-knit, experienced and highly committed team. The culture is professional while informal, collegial and service-focused, with strong respect for cultural identity, relationships and mutual support. Given the often demanding nature of the work, empathy, humour and resilience are important.
The successful GM will be a grounded, emotionally mature leader who builds trust, listens well and values diverse cultures and life experiences. A highly corporate or hierarchical style will not suit; this role calls for someone accessible, practical and willing to roll up their sleeves when needed.

Benefits
  • Lead a financially stable organisation with a clear social purpose and tangible impact on access to justice, with core government funding secured through June 2028.
  • Work with a highly experienced, committed and culturally diverse team with a strong record of retention.
  • Help shape the next strategic phase, including succession, service development, technology and responsible use of AI, while building influence across the community law, justice, government and social service sectors.  
How to Apply

If you are motivated by meaningful community impact and believe your leadership style fits this distinctive environment, we would welcome your application. Please click the “APPLY” button to submit your CV and cover letter.

For a confidential discussion, contact Kirsten Edwards on +64 9 915 9140 or Iain MacGibbon on +64 9 915 9144.

job.title: Clinical Manager, Aged Care - Wellington Central
job.description:
Are you a proven Clinical Manager or a Registered Nurse with solid people management skills, based in Wellington or considering a move, with the type of personality that resonates and motivates people?  Want to work for a leader in the retirement village sector, one that invests in its people and puts the welfare of its residents first? We would urge you to consider this career option.

We are seeking a strong and natural leader to join our senior leadership team as we work together to foster a care delivery culture that supports the values and purpose of our aged community. 

If you are passionate about measurable and meaningful quality of care that meets contractual and legislative requirements and reflects current best practices, this is the opportunity for you.

You will lead a passionate team committed to supporting our aged care residents to live life their way.

This is a full-time role working Monday to Friday with some on-call requirements during evenings and weekends.

Qualifications
Our ideal candidate must have
  • At least 5 years of experience working as a registered nurse with a passion for aged care (and a current NZ annual practicing certificate).
  • Be committed to holistic person-centered care.
  • Have a calm and measured approach - able to problem solve and adapt to an ever-changing environment.
  • Be an effective and respectful communicator; highly skilled in written, oral, and interpersonal communication. 
  • Be able to build strong relationships with your team, residents, and whanau
  • Have experience with leading a team, including recruitment and development of staff and managing rosters.
  • Have strong organisational and time management skills.
  • Be InterRAI trained.
  • Engage with all our professional stakeholders to build strong local relationships.
  • Be resilient and committed to self-care.
Additional Information
What we can offer
  • A competitive market rate
  • An engaging and positive work environment
  • Ongoing professional development
  • Professional supervision
  • To become a part of the nationwide village community
  • Support to complete post-graduate study
  • A great local leadership team and ongoing mentorship
If you are looking for a role with a real sense of purpose and the opportunity to genuinely make a difference, this is the role for you! Please use the APPLY NOW button to progress your application or call Rhys Holding, Farrow Jamieson on +64 9 915 9147 for a confidential chat.

job.title: Accountant
job.description:
Accountant - Put your financial expertise to work where it makes a difference.

Farrow Jamieson is partnering with an established Auckland-based, Christian organisation whose work is grounded in faith and a strong commitment to making a positive difference in the lives of others.

There is a genuine sense of purpose behind the organisation and the way it operates. Stewardship, service, compassion and community are important to the culture, and finance plays a key role in ensuring resources are used thoughtfully and responsibly.

The team is close-knit, practical and busy, with supportive leadership, genuine flexibility and people who care about both the quality of their work and the wider impact it enables.

About the Role
A broad Senior Accountant role with a strong management accounting and business partnering focus. Reporting to the COO, you will work across the organisation to bring clarity to financial information, strengthen planning and help managers make well-informed decisions.

The scope goes well beyond a narrow month-end role. You will move between financial accounting, reporting, budgeting, forecasting, audit coordination, analysis and process improvement. It will suit someone who enjoys variety, likes being close to the business and is comfortable getting into the detail when needed.

Duties
  • Own budgeting, forecasting and regular reforecasting across the organisation.
  • Deliver accurate monthly and annual reporting, including variance analysis and commentary.
  • Prepare annual financial accounts, GST returns and key reconciliations.
  • Coordinate audit requirements and work confidently with external advisers.
  • Oversee payroll and support core accounts receivable and payable processes.
  • Partner with managers to improve financial understanding, planning and resource allocation.
  • Contribute to project and funding-related financial planning and business cases.
  • Help strengthen finance systems, policies, processes and ways of working.
Skills & Experience
You will be a capable accountant who brings both technical strength and the confidence to work with people outside finance. Not-for-profit experience is useful, but it is not essential; a broad commercial accounting background can work equally well.
  • At least four years of post-graduate accounting experience in New Zealand.
  • CA qualified, or well progressed towards completing your qualification.
  • Strong management accounting, budgeting, forecasting and reporting experience.
  • Sound financial accounting knowledge, including GST, audit and reconciliations.
  • Strong Excel skills and confidence working with accounting systems.
  • Proven ability to partner with managers and explain finance in plain language.
  • A practical, adaptable style and an interest in improving how things are done.
Culture
This is a genuinely faith-led workplace. Service, integrity, thoughtful stewardship and a sense of community matter here, and people are encouraged to bring both capability and care to their work.

You will suit the environment if you enjoy collaborating, are willing to contribute beyond a narrow job description and like the idea of using your finance skills in an organisation with a strong sense of purpose. It is a busy role, so you will also need to be comfortable juggling priorities and taking ownership.

Benefits
  • Salary up to $110,000.
  • Genuine hybrid working flexibility for part of the week.
  • Free onsite parking.
  • Medical insurance.
  • Direct exposure to senior leadership and a broad view of the organisation.
  • The opportunity to shape processes and grow with the role over time.
  • Inspiring weekly team devotions for spritual growth.
How to Apply
If you are looking for a Senior Accountant role with real breadth, strong business partnering and want to use your professional skills in a Christian organisation committed to serving others and making a difference, we would be keen to hear from you.

Click the “APPLY” button to submit your application. Along with your CV, please provide a cover letter explaining why you’re interested in this working in this organisation.

For a confidential discussion, contact Amanda at Farrow Jamieson on +64 9 915 9142

job.title: Operations Manager, Public Transport - North Shore
job.description:
About the Opportunity
Our client is a well-established New Zealand public transport operator providing essential services to communities every day.

An opportunity has become available for an experienced Operations Manager to lead the day-to-day performance of a busy depot. You'll be responsible for ensuring services run safely, efficiently and reliably while leading a team of drivers, cleaners and yard staff.

This is a hands-on operational leadership role where no two days are the same. Success comes from strong planning, calm decision-making, genuine people leadership and a commitment to delivering outstanding customer service.

About the Role
Reporting to the Area Manager, you'll oversee the daily operation of the depot and provide leadership to a team of frontline employees.

You'll coordinate people, vehicles and resources to ensure services operate safely and on time while responding to the changing demands that come with running a customer-facing transport operation.

Alongside the day-to-day operation, you'll coach your team, manage performance, support recruitment and training, monitor operational KPIs and foster a culture where safety and accountability come first.

NOTE: This ad is not a re-post of the same recent advertisement, but the same job at a different depot.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead, coach and support drivers, cleaners and yard staff.
  • Manage daily rosters and operational resources.
  • Respond to operational issues and service disruptions.
  • Promote a positive safety culture and lead incident response.
  • Monitor operational performance and depot KPIs.
  • Develop employees through coaching, feedback and training.
  • Build strong working relationships with customers and internal teams.
  • Ensure compliance with company policies and regulatory requirements.
  • Drive continuous improvement across depot operations.
About You
You're an experienced frontline leader who enjoys working with people and thrives in a fast-moving operational environment.

You'll bring:
  • Experience leading blue-collar or frontline operational teams.
  • Strong organisational and planning skills.
  • The ability to make sound decisions under pressure.
  • A genuine commitment to Health & Safety.
  • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
  • Experience improving operational performance and team engagement.
  • A practical, hands-on leadership style.
  • High attention to detail and strong personal accountability.
Experience within public transport would be highly regarded. We also welcome applications from leaders who have developed their careers in logistics, freight, distribution, courier, warehousing, manufacturing or other operational environments where safety, scheduling, customer service and people leadership are central to success.

Why Apply?
This is an opportunity to join a stable, well-established organisation providing an essential public service.

You'll lead a close-knit operational team, have genuine influence over depot performance and play an important role in delivering reliable services to the local community.

Please use the APPLY NOW button to progress your application or call Rhys Holding of Farrow Jamieson on +64 9 915 9147 for a confidential chat.
